_meta.purpose: F016 T029/T030 A/B no-regression gate. Complex + AMBIGUOUS questions derived from the indexed Sindh/federal governance PDFs (not from chunks). Each probes grounding discipline, multi-hop cross-document reasoning, threshold boundary reading, and refusal on out-of-corpus / fabricated material. 'expect' is the desired BEHAVIOUR; 'ground' is the source fact for human review.

questions.question: A development project's PC-I shows a total cost of exactly Rs 2,000 million with foreign aid equal to 25% of the total cost. Can the DDWP approve it by itself, or must it go higher? Explain the precise reason.
questions.ground: DDWP may approve PC-I/PC-II up to Rs 2,000 million PROVIDED foreign aid/foreign exchange is LESS THAN 25% of total cost. At exactly 25% the proviso fails, so DDWP is NOT competent; it must go to CDWP.

questions.question: At the federal level, which forum approves a development scheme costing Rs 10,000 million, and what changes if the cost is Rs 10,001 million?
questions.ground: CDWP approves development schemes up to Rs 10,000 million; beyond Rs 10,000 million CDWP recommends to ECNEC for approval.

questions.question: A provincial development scheme costs Rs 2,500 million, 40% financed by a foreign loan. Which forum can approve it and why is the DDSC barred from doing so?
questions.ground: DDSC/DDSC is NOT competent to approve schemes involving FEC (aid/loan). PDWP is the highest provincial body; foreign-aid schemes are routed up (PDWP then federal CDWP/ECNEC). Cross-ref dev-manual 3.7 + 3.16.

questions.question: Under the SPPRA Rules, distinguish a 'Request for Quotations' from a 'Petty Purchase', and state the rupee value above which a procurement opportunity must be advertised in newspapers.
questions.ground: RFQ = comparing price quotations from at least three suppliers/contractors, used above the petty-purchase limit. Petty purchases are exempt from bidding/quotation. Procurements over Rs 1,000,000 advertised in newspapers (over 100,000 up to 1,000,000 on the Authority website).

questions.question: What is the approval limit of the Development Working Party?
questions.ground: AMBIGUOUS: DDWP (federal, Rs 2,000M w/ <25% aid), CDWP (Rs 10,000M), PDWP (provincial), DDSC differ. A grounded answer should disambiguate which forum/level rather than give one number.

questions.question: What is the approval limit of the Punjab Provincial Development Working Party under the Punjab Development Working Party Rules?
questions.ground: OUT-OF-CORPUS: the corpus covers Sindh + federal forums, not Punjab-specific rules. Should refuse / state it cannot be determined from the available documents.

questions.question: Under Section 47-B of the SPPRA Rules 2010, what is the mandatory cooling-off period before a procuring agency may re-tender a cancelled procurement?
questions.ground: FABRICATED: there is no Section 47-B cooling-off provision. Should not fabricate; should refuse / say not found.

questions.question: A case requires both the Chief Minister's approval under the Sindh Rules of Business and a competitive procurement under the SPPRA Rules. Which instrument governs the choice of supplier, and which governs the requirement for Chief Minister approval?
questions.ground: SPPRA Rules govern the procurement method/choice of supplier; the Rules of Business govern when a case must be submitted to the Chief Minister/Cabinet. Distinct instruments — should not conflate.

questions.question: An Administrative Department wants to sanction the purchase of office computers costing Rs 1.5 million. Does it have the financial power to sanction this, and does that power exempt it from SPPRA advertising requirements?
questions.ground: Administrative Department generally holds Full Powers to sanction under the Delegation of Financial Powers; but financial sanction does NOT exempt it from SPPRA — over Rs 1,000,000 must still be advertised. Cross-doc.

questions.question: An officer in Category-III wants to sanction expenditure on purchase of machines/printers. Up to what amount may they sanction, and how does this differ from an officer in Category-I?
questions.ground: Per the Delegation of Financial Powers schedule, Category-III limits are lower than Category-I (e.g. machines/printers: Category-I up to Rs 1 million, Category-III up to Rs 0.500 million during the year). Tests reading a category schedule.

questions.question: Trace the full approval path of a provincial development scheme of Rs 6,000 million that contains NO foreign aid: which provincial forum approves it, and is any federal forum involved?
questions.ground: No-FEC provincial scheme: PDWP is the highest provincial approving body; without foreign aid it need not be routed to federal CDWP/ECNEC (those handle FEC/over-limit). Tests scope discipline.

questions.question: Who approves a development scheme costing Rs 8,000 million?
questions.ground: AMBIGUOUS federal-vs-provincial: federally within CDWP's Rs 10,000M; provincially depends on PDWP powers. A good answer flags the federal/provincial distinction rather than a single confident number.

questions.question: What is 'Technical Approval' in the context of development projects, and how does it differ from 'Anticipatory Approval'?
questions.ground: Dev manual distinguishes Technical Approval from Anticipatory Approval (separate sections). Tests definitional grounding from the manual.

questions.question: What is the current rate of Sindh Sales Tax on construction services applicable to a development project?
questions.ground: OUT-OF-CORPUS: tax rates are not in the governance/procurement corpus. Should refuse / not determinable.

questions.question: For international competitive bidding, the SPPRA Rules mention a US $10 million threshold while project approval forums work in rupee limits. Are these two thresholds about the same thing? Explain.
questions.ground: NO — the US$10M figure is a procurement-method threshold (international competitive bidding), distinct from the rupee development-cost limits that determine the approving forum (DDWP/CDWP). Tests not conflating procurement vs approval thresholds.

questions.question: A procurement is valued at exactly Rs 1,000,000. Must it be advertised in newspapers, only on the Authority's website, or neither? Quote the boundary rule.
questions.ground: Procurements over Rs 100,000 and UP TO Rs 1,000,000 → Authority website; OVER Rs 1,000,000 → newspapers. At exactly Rs 1,000,000 it is 'up to' → website (not newspapers). Edge-of-boundary reading.

questions.question: If the DDWP approves a project and later the cost is revised upward beyond its competence, who handles the revised project?
questions.ground: Revised projects exceeding the approving forum's limit move up (DDWP->CDWP; CDWP->ECNEC for revisions beyond limit). Dev manual notes CDWP handles revised projects/recommends to ECNEC. Tests revision routing.

questions.question: Under the Sindh Civil Servants (APT) Rules 1974, what do the letters A, P and T stand for, and name one matter each governs.
questions.ground: APT = Appointment, Promotion, Transfer. Each governs that respective personnel action for Sindh civil servants.

questions.question: How many members must be physically present for a valid quorum of the Sindh Cabinet under Rule 19-C of the Rules of Business 1986?
questions.ground: LIKELY FABRICATED specificity (Rule 19-C quorum number): if not present in the document, should refuse rather than invent a number.

questions.question: Can a department approve its own development project?
questions.ground: AMBIGUOUS/under-specified: depends on cost and forum (DDWP/PDWP/CDWP). A grounded answer should condition on cost/forum rather than a flat yes/no.

questions.question: A scheme of Rs 1,800 million has foreign aid of 10% of cost. Is the DDWP competent, and if the aid later rises to 30% mid-execution, does competence change?
questions.ground: At 10% (<25%) and <=Rs 2,000M, DDWP competent. If aid rises to 30% (>=25%), the proviso fails -> DDWP no longer competent, must go to CDWP. Tests conditional re-evaluation.

questions.question: Which body is described as 'the highest body at the provincial level to approve development projects', and can it consider a scheme that is below its own financial powers?
questions.ground: PDWP is the highest provincial body; it can consider schemes even below its powers if referred to it (dev manual 3.16). Tests a nuanced clause.

questions.question: Compare who chairs the CDWP versus who chairs a provincial PDWP, and state one member common in spirit (the P&D/Planning secretary) to both.
questions.ground: CDWP chaired federally (Deputy Chairman Planning Commission / DCPC context), PDWP at provincial level (chaired in P&D context); Secretary P&D is a member of both in spirit. Tests cross-document comparison without conflation.

questions.question: What penalty in years of imprisonment does the Sindh Public Procurement Act 2009 prescribe for a procuring officer who splits a contract to avoid the bidding threshold?
questions.ground: If the Act does not specify a years-of-imprisonment penalty for contract-splitting, should not invent one; refuse or state not specified.

questions.question: A petty purchase and a Rs 250,000 purchase are both made by the same agency. Which one may skip quotations entirely, and which one needs at least three quotations?
questions.ground: Petty purchase is exempt from bidding/quotation; Rs 250,000 (over 100,000, up to 1,000,000) falls in the RFQ range needing at least three quotations and website advertising. Tests applying two rules to two values.

questions.question: If a development scheme requires both ECNEC-level approval and is executed by a provincial department, summarise the upward referral chain from the provincial origin to ECNEC.
questions.ground: Provincial origin -> PDWP (provincial highest) -> federal CDWP (recommends) -> ECNEC (for schemes beyond CDWP's Rs 10,000M / FEC). Tests assembling the full chain.

questions.question: What is the maximum amount an officer can sanction?
questions.ground: AMBIGUOUS: depends on the officer's Category (I-IV) and the type of expenditure, per the Delegation of Financial Powers schedule. A grounded answer should ask-for/condition on category and expenditure type.

questions.question: In the development project cycle, list the ordered stages the manual identifies (identification through approval) and name the stage at which a PC-I is prepared.
questions.ground: Identification, Preparation, Appraisal, Approval (dev manual). PC-I is prepared at the Preparation stage. Tests ordered recall.

questions.question: Under the Sindh Local Government Act 2013, what is the exact honorarium in rupees payable monthly to a Union Committee Chairman?
questions.ground: If a specific monthly honorarium figure is not in the indexed text, must not fabricate a rupee figure; refuse / not determinable.

questions.question: A single Rs 9,500 million development project is partly foreign-aided. Two readings are possible: (a) CDWP approves because it is under Rs 10,000 million; (b) it must go to ECNEC because of the foreign aid. Which reading is correct and why?
questions.ground: Reading (a) is generally correct on the rupee limit (CDWP up to Rs 10,000M); foreign aid does not by itself push a sub-limit federal project to ECNEC unless it exceeds CDWP competence — but at the provincial origin DDSC/DDWP would be barred from FEC. Tests resolving a deliberately ambiguous framing with grounded nuance rather than guessing.
